News.title: SpaceX Starship V3 launch live: How to watch 'most powerful rocket ever' blast off
News.content:
Tonight's launch will mark a significant step in plans to use the Starship to visit Mars

The new version of SpaceX's Starship craft, designed to carry both crew and cargo to the Moon, Mars, and beyond, is due to blast off on a crucial test flight in an hour's time

SpaceX Starship V3 launch live: How to watch 'most powerful rocket ever' blast off

The countdown has started ahead of the launch of the most powerful SpaceX rocket ever built that may one day take humans to Mars.

Elon Musk’s spaceflight company is set to launch the 12th test flight of the Starship spacecraft, which is intended to launch dummy satellites and do a flip during the hour-long planned flight.

If today’s flight goes smoothly the rocket may be one step closer to Musk’s aim of sending a Starship to Mars by the end of 2026. A live stream of the launch will be available on the Mirror website.

News.title: UK heatwave live: Met Office forecasts 33C weather as areas facing heat revealed
News.content:
Anomaly maps reveal temperatures will rise well above the seasonal average over the Bank Holiday weekend

Met Office weather forecasters expect record-breaking 33C temperatures over the Bank Holiday weekend as an official heatwave should be declared in four parts of the UK

Temperatures could rise to 33C over the Bank Holiday weekend as Met Office weather forecasters predict an official heatwave.

The national weather agency reckons the mercury could to 30C on Saturday, followed by 32C on Sunday and a sweltering 33C on Monday - which would be the hottest ever temperature for May. The current record is 32.8C.

The south-east of England is expected to be the hottest region, although official heatwave conditions could also be reached in central England, western England and parts of Wales, according to the Met Office.

An official heatwave is declared when temperatures rise above the heatwave threshold for three consecutive days. The threshold varies from 25C to 28C across different counties.

News.title: Lee Andrews LIVE: Katie Price issues update saying 'I'm still looking for answers'
News.content:
Katie Price has taken to social media to share her thoughts in a late-night posting spree as the search for her husband enters its second week, with the saga only getting more confusing as time goes on

Katie Price was forced to cut her podcast short after her sister said she'd received a call from the police. Her sister Sophie revealed Katie had go, saying: "Kate has had to shoot off because she is taking a call from the police, so that is it for today's episode."

It comes after Katie 47, took to social media to share a series of pointed quotes in a late-night posting spree, with the no-context posts leading some to wonder if they have anything to do with her 'kidnapped' husband Lee Andrews.

Katie shared her final texts from her husband Lee Andrews on Tuesday fearing he has been 'kidnapped', saying she had no idea how long this would last: "I don’t know if this is going to go on for weeks, months, years, or never."

She raised the alarm last Thursday, revealing that no one had heard from Lee since Wednesday evening: "Lee was trying to get through the boarder at Hatta, this is so discombobulating, his location went off at 10.03pm on Wednesday night, that’s the last contact anyone has had – his family and myself. This is the third day now."

News.title: Police find body in Stoke-on-Trent woods during hunt for Tyler, 14
News.content:
Police find body in Stoke-on-Trent woods during hunt for Tyler, 14

A body believed to be that of missing schoolboy Tyler Townsend has been discovered near Burslem Cemetery in Stoke-on-Trent, after the 14-year-old was last seen on Sunday, 17 May

View Image Tyler Townsend

A body has been discovered during the search for a missing 14 year old schoolboy.

‌



Officers had been hunting for Tyler Townsend since Sunday, 17 May.

‌



The search came to a tragic end on Thursday evening when Tyler's body was believed to have been found near Burslem Cemetery.

‌



A Staffordshire Police spokesman said: "We can sadly confirm that a body has been found in the search for missing 14-year-old Tyler, from Stoke-on-Trent.

He was last seen in the area on Sunday (17 May). Officers have been carrying out extensive searches to try to find him since he was reported missing. Shortly after 7pm today (Thursday 21 May), a body was found in a wooded area near Burslem Cemetery.

Article continues below

"Formal identification will take place in due course, but we believe the body to be missing boy Tyler. Officers are supporting his family at this deeply distressing time. His death is not being treated as suspicious and a file will be prepared for HM Coroner."

StokeonTrentLive has contacted West Midlands Ambulance Service for a comment following the heartbreaking incident.

News.title: Boys' sentences for rape slammed by police and crime commissioner as 'too lenient'
News.content:
Boys' sentences for rape slammed by police and crime commissioner as 'too lenient'

The three teenage boys, two aged 15 and one aged 14, avoided prison sentences after raping two girls in separate incidents several weeks apart and filming the attacks

View 3 Images Hampshire and the Isle of Wight Police and Crime Commissioner Donna Jones said the sentences were 'far too lenient' (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Express)

A police and crime commissioner has slammed a court's 'lenient' sentence after three teenage boys avoided jail for raping two girls and 'brazenly' filming the attacks.

Donna Jones, Police and Crime Commissioner for Hampshire and Isle of Wight, said that she was concerned that the boys could commit such "terrifying acts" and not face a custodial sentence.

The trial at Southampton Crown Court heard that two girls were raped in two separate incidents in Fordingbridge, Hampshire, with the first attack on November 26, 2024 and the second on January 17, 2025. The three boys, two aged 15 and one aged 14, were handed youth rehabilitation orders (YRO) and the two older ones were also made subject to intensive supervision and surveillance (ISS) - but were not given prison sentences.

View 3 Images One of the girls was attacked in an underpass beside the River Avon

Ms Jones said she would support the families of the victims if they sought to appeal against the "leniency" of the sentences, commenting: "This is an extremely disturbing case. I'm deeply concerned these boys felt they could carry out such terrifying acts and share them online and not go to prison. "Their sentences reflect a clear focus on rehabilitation rather than criminalisation. They are far too lenient. As they stand, they offer little comfort to their victims as they try to rebuild their lives after such harrowing experiences. "Should the victims and their families take the decision to appeal the sentences, I will offer my support. The education of young people about sexual violence and misogynistic attitudes is vitally important if we're to prevent crimes like this from happening again. My thoughts remain with the two young girls and their families." A 15-year-old boy was sentenced to a three-year YRO with 180 days of ISS for the rape of each of the two girls and two indecent images charges. The court heard that he had been diagnosed with ADHD as well as "long-standing anxiety".

Article continues below

A second 15-year-old was given the same sentence for three charges of rape against each of the two victims and four counts of taking indecent images in relation to filming of the incidents. The court was told that he had an IQ of the "bottom 1% of his contemporaries" and had been diagnosed with ADHD.

View 3 Images The case was heard at Southampton Crown Court (Image: PA Archive/PA Images)

A third boy, aged 14, was given a YRO for 18 months for two charges of rape in the January incident by encouraging the second defendant and an offence of indecent images. He was described as having "mild cognitive impairment". Judge Nicholas Rowland told the defendants: "I have to remember that you are not small adults. I have to think how likely you are to do serious things again and I need to make sure you do not do serious things again in the future." Explaining his sentence, he added: "I should avoid criminalising these children unnecessarily and understand the effects of their behaviour and support their reintegration into society." He added that "peer pressure played a large part in what went on". The victim of the first incident came to the court for the sentencing hearing and, screened from the view of the boys, read her victim impact statement as well as a poem she had written directed towards her attackers. She described how her mental health had deteriorated since the incident leading her to isolate herself from her friends. She said: "I was caught off-guard, I never want that to happen again, I will never get that innocence back again." The poem included the line: "All I want to do is die, I no longer have fear for when that comes." She added: "No-one deserves the trauma of being raped." In a statement read on behalf of the second victim, she said her school attendance had suffered and added: "I often feel overwhelmed, anxious and emotionally exhausted to the point where sitting in a classroom becomes unbearable." She described suffering nightmares and struggling to sleep and added: "I feel ashamed, insecure and uncomfortable in my own body." She added: "The person I was before the incident has completely gone and sometimes I feel like I am grieving the person I used to be." The judge praised the bravery of the two girls for providing their statements and giving evidence and said to the first victim: "I hope when you look back on today's date you will take some comfort from the fact you have shown that courage in coming along to court. You and (the second girl) have shown great courage in coming along to the trial and speaking as you did." He added: "The sentence I am going to pass cannot possibly undo what happened to you." The boys were also made subject to a three-month curfew and given a restraining order for 10 years not to contact their victims. Jodie Mittel KC, prosecuting, told the trial that the girl in the November incident, who was 15 at the time, had visited the first defendant after meeting him on Snapchat. The prosecutor said that after performing sex acts on the boy, who was then 14, she became "scared and anxious" when the second defendant joined them with a third boy who was not charged. Ms Mittel said that the girl felt "cornered and trapped" and "petrified" as the two defendants raped her while the incident was filmed. Ms Mittel said that afterwards, videos of the incident had been sent around and other people made jokes about her and she received messages calling her a "slag". The victim in the January incident, who was 14 at the time, was raped in a field near to Fordingbridge recreation ground while the incident was also filmed. Siobhan Blake, the Crown Prosecution Service's national lead for rape and serious sexual offences (RASSO), said: "It is vital young people are educated and informed about consent and that harmful and misogynistic attitudes are tackled as early as possible to prevent these crimes. Everyone has a part to play. "Young people must understand that sexual activity without consent is a serious criminal offence that can lead to them being prosecuted."

News.title: Iran war live: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei risks Trump fury with uranium demand
News.content:
Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered the country's near-weapons-grade uranium is not sent abroad - but Donald Trump has threatened to hit Iran 'even harder' if Tehran does not agree to his demands

Iran's Supreme Leader Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei has ordered Iran's near-weapons-grade uranium stay in the country, according to two senior Iranian sources - a move expected to further anger Donald Trump.

The US President has threatened to hit Iran "even harder" and get a "little bit nasty" if a peace deal is not reached soon - with all US demands so far aimed at preventing Tehran from acquiring a nuclear weapon.

"We hit them very hard. We may have to hit them even harder - but maybe not," Trump said during an address at the US Coast Guard Academy yesterday. "But we're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon and blow up the entire Middle East, Israel, the entire Middle East, and then come here for you. Not going to happen."

Benjamin Netanyahu has said he will not consider the war over until enriched uranium is removed from Iran.

News.title: Missing boys found alone and crying on roadside as 'mum' arrested 110 miles away
News.content:
Missing boys found alone and crying on roadside as 'mum' arrested 110 miles away

A man and a woman have been arrested after two children, both aged under five, who were discovered crying and alone by the side of a road in Portugal

View 3 Images The two boys were found crying and alone by the side of a road (Image: GNR)

A man and woman have been arrested after two children were found crying and alone by the side of a road in southern Portugal.

‌



Local media reports the couple were the mother and stepfather of the two French boys. The children, both aged under five, were discovered by a driver near the southern Portuguese town of Alcacer do Sal on Tuesday, police said.

‌



The youngsters were carrying backpacks when they were found, which contained food and water, but they had no identity documents.

‌



The pair were reported missing by their father from their home in Colmar in eastern France on May 11, leading to a pan-European request for help being issued by French authorities.

View 3 Images The youngsters were found beside a road (Image: GNR)

‌

Police in both Portugal and France are investigating how the boys ended up beside the road, but so far they have not reached any conclusions.

The couple were arrested after local police swooped when their car was spotted outside a café in the city of Fatima, about 180km (112miles) north of Alcacer do Sal where the boys were found.

View 3 Images The pair were found with backpacks containing food and water (Image: GNR)

Article continues below

A 41-year-old woman and man aged 55 were being held, Portugal's National Republican Guard said. The arrested pair have not been formally identified by authorities.

They said the couple were being investigated for the crimes of domestic violence, exposure to danger, and abandonment.

The driver who first came across the two boys has said he fed them before alerting the police.

News.title: Foden and Palmer to miss out on World Cup squad
News.content:
Phil Foden and Cole Palmer are set to miss out when Thomas Tuchel names his 26-man England squad on Friday for this summer's World Cup.

Manchester United defender Harry Maguire will also be left out, with the 33-year-old saying he is "shocked and gutted" at the decision.

Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is set to be included - after helping his side win the Europa League on Wednesday - alongside Al-Ahli striker Ivan Toney, who has scored 32 goals in 32 games in the Saudi Arabian league this season.

Nottingham Forest midfielder Morgan Gibbs-White is set to miss out, despite being the top-scoring English player in the Premier League this season, alongside Watkins and Dominic Calvert-Lewin, on 14 goals.

Manchester City's Foden and Chelsea's Palmer - both attacking midfielders who can also play as forwards - have had inconsistent seasons for their respective clubs.

In a post on Instagram, Maguire confirmed: "I was confident I could have played a major part this summer for my country after the season I've had. I've been left shocked and gutted by the decision. I wish the players all the best."

Maguire's mother Zoe posted on social media to express her disappointment, saying she was "disgusted" by the decision.

Maguire's Manchester United team-mate Luke Shaw is also set to be omitted despite his impressive season.

News.title: Flares light up Aston Villa's Europa League victory parade
News.content:
Thousands of Aston Villa fans lined the streets of Birmingham's to celebrate the club's Europa League victory.

Three open top busses carried club's players and staff through the city centre, as jubilant fans turned out with flags and flares to celebrate its first major European trophy since 1982.

The squad lifted the Europa League trophy to cheers in a packed Centenary Square, which the city council says was at full capacity.

Aston Villa ended a 30-year trophy drought on Wednesday with a 3-0 victory over Freiburg at Istanbul's Besiktas Park.

News.title: NASCAR driver Kyle Busch dies at 41
News.content:
Two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Kyle Busch has died at 41 after being hospitalized with a severe illness, his family announced on Thursday.

“Our entire NASCAR family is heartbroken by the loss of Kyle Busch,” the Busch Family, Richard Childress Racing and NASCAR said in a joint statement that Busch died after being hospitalized.

“Throughout a career that spanned more than two decades, Kyle set records in national series wins, won championships at NASCAR’s highest level and fostered the next generation of drivers as an owner in the Truck Series. His sharp wit and competitive spirit sparked a deep emotional connection with race fans of every age, creating the proud and loyal ‘Rowdy Nation,’” the statement said.

This marks the first time in over a decade that Busch has been absent from a Cup Series race, with his last significant absence occurring in 2015 due to injuries.

Busch, a formidable figure in NASCAR with 234 career wins, is ranked 24th in the Cup Series standings this season.

Two-time NASCAR Cup Series champion Kyle Busch died at 41, his family announced on Thursday.

“Our entire NASCAR family is heartbroken by the loss of Kyle Busch,” the Busch Family, Richard Childress Racing and NASCAR said in a joint statement that Busch died after being hospitalized.

“A future Hall of Famer, Kyle was a rare talent, one who comes along once in a generation. He was fierce, he was passionate, he was immensely skilled and he cared deeply about the sport and fans.”

“Throughout a career that spanned more than two decades, Kyle set records in national series wins, won championships at NASCAR’s highest level and fostered the next generation of drivers as an owner in the Truck Series. His sharp wit and competitive spirit sparked a deep emotional connection with race fans of every age, creating the proud and loyal ‘Rowdy Nation,’” the statement said.

No cause of death was given.

His family shared an update on social media early on Thursday, stating that Busch was currently undergoing treatment and would miss the Coca-Cola 600 over the weekend.

They asked for discretion, saying, "We ask for understanding and privacy as our family navigates this situation."

Busch, a Las Vegas native, was a formidable presence in NASCAR, having secured championships in 2015 and 2019.

Known for his polarizing personality, he holds the record for the most wins across the sport's three national series, with 234 victories, including 63 Cup Series races.

This season, his fourth with Richard Childress Racing after a successful tenure at Joe Gibbs Racing, has seen him rank 24th in the Cup Series standings with two top-10 finishes in 12 races. His last victory came in 2023, his inaugural win with RCR.

This marks the first time in over a decade that Busch has been absent from a Cup Series race ( Getty )

Busch's current season has been marked by struggles for consistency since his move to RCR, a period that also saw a public spat with his former Joe Gibbs Racing teammate, Denny Hamlin.

Hamlin had appeared to criticize Busch on his "Actions Detrimental" podcast, remarking, "If you’re expecting Kyle Busch to just go back to Victory Lane on a regular basis, you are kidding yourselves."

Busch took exception to these comments, despite Hamlin later claiming he meant no harm. The tension escalated at last month’s race in Kansas, where Busch, several laps down, aggressively raced Hamlin, who was leading. This move significantly held up Hamlin during a critical phase of the race, ultimately contributing to Tyler Reddick’s victory, while Hamlin, despite leading 131 laps, faded to fourth.

However, the two drivers appear to have since mended their relationship, with Hamlin publicly acknowledging Busch as being on the "Mount Rushmore" of racing.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom is in a spat with a major oil company over who is to blame for the state's high gas prices, with the Democratic governor's office urging drivers not to fill up at Chevron stations over Memorial Day weekend.

“Pro tip: unbranded gas comes from the same refineries, storage tanks, and pipelines, and it meets the same state standards to keep your engine running clean,” Newsom’s office posted Thursday on X. “Big Oil is already making billions off Trump’s Iran War; don’t let them rip you off even more by overpaying for the brand name.”

Newsom’s office cited an analysis by a group within the state's energy commission, which oversees the oil and gas industry, that found that Chevron averaged more than 60 to 80 cents per gallon above unbranded alternatives.

The call-out follows Chevron posting signs at California gas stations blaming the state's climate policies for the high cost of gas. The average price of gas in California sat at $6.14 per gallon on Thursday, about $1.58 higher than the national average, according to the American Automobile Association. The state taxes consumers about 70 cents per gallon of gas, according to the state’s energy commission. That is the highest gas tax in the country.

“California politicians are choosing foreign oil and fuels over local jobs and lower costs,” the signs read. They feature a QR code that directs to a Chevron webpage asking people to “speak up for affordable, reliable energy.”

It is not clear when Chevron put the signs up, but spokesman Ross Allen said they are part of a campaign the company launched three years ago to inform drivers on the price impacts of California policies.

“We've been very vocal about the importance of customer education in California so that our drivers and our consumers understand where their tax dollars are going,” Allen said.

There are hundreds of Chevron gas stations operating in California, and most of them are operated independently and set their own prices, he said.

Memorial Day is typically one of the busiest travel weekends of the year.

Prices at the pump have swelled nationwide since the Iran war began, launching a global energy crisis. The price of crude oil, which is the main ingredient in gasoline, has climbed during the war because the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow passage of the Persian Gulf through which a fifth of the world’s crude oil normally passes, has effectively been shut. Oil tankers have been stranded there unable to deliver crude.

Newsom, who often touts the state's status as a global climate leader, has passed policies in recent years aimed at cracking down on oil company profits and reducing gas prices.

He signed a law in 2023 allowing the state's energy commission to penalize oil companies for excess profits, declaring the state had “finally beat big oil.” But regulators voted last year to hold off on plans to penalize businesses until 2030 and prioritize other efforts to protect consumers at the pump.

The postponement came after two oil refineries that accounted for roughly 18% of the state's refining capacity announced their plans to close, reigniting debate over the price impacts of the state's ambitious climate policies.

Newsom signed another law in 2024 giving the commission the authority to require refineries to keep a certain amount of fuel on hand. The goal is to try to keep prices from increasing suddenly when refineries go offline for maintenance. But that regulation has also stalled.

The Senate left town on Thursday without beginning votes on legislation that the GOP plans to push through the filibuster-proof reconciliation process to fund ICE enforcement and removal operations.

And it was all thanks to Republicans arguing amongst themselves over the president’s plans for a White House ballroom and a $1.776 billion “slush fund” for Trump’s allies.

Senators who spoke to The Independent coming out of a GOP luncheon on Thursday confirmed that plans for a “vote-a-rama” overnight session were being spiked until after the Memorial Day holiday, and lawmakers quickly began filing out of the Capitol after the news.

Even a desperate, last-minute visit from Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to drum up support among the Senate Republican caucus appeared to net few results.

Sen. Lisa Murkowski departed the meeting and told reporters that skepticism to the “slush fund,” as critics have labeled the DOJ settlement with Trump, remained high. “Let’s just say it was a very fulsome, important discussion with the White House — and nobody held back,” the Alaska senator said, when asked whether this moment marked an instance where Republican senators would finally assert their independence from the president.

open image in gallery Senate Majority Leader John Thune has expressed his skepticism towards supporting the DOJ’s nearly $1.8B ‘slush fund’ for prosecuted allies of Trump ( AP )

Senate Majority Leader John Thune, meanwhile, had little to say to reporters as he hurried out of that meeting on Thursday, but seemingly confirmed that the demand for the inclusion of the weaponization fund was the reason for the holdup.

“It’s a big issue,” Thune said of the so-called “weaponization’ fund.

Thune, who has been under fire from Trump, also said he hadn’t spoken with the president as the Senate prepared to skip town.

As lawmakers fled the Senate, their colleagues in the House unveiled a bipartisan amendment aimed at killing the fund that they plan to tack on to the reconciliation bill.

Sen. Thom Tillis lambasted the fund on Wednesday, and Thune had previously indicated his own lukewarm feelings — indicating that the White House may be fighting a losing battle.

Many lawmakers complained openly about the lack of concrete guardrails around the fund, which was unveiled by Blanche at the Department of Justice as a means of compensating people “unfairly” targeted for prosecution by the Biden Justice Department. The fund would use taxpayer money, and critics say it could be used to benefit the scores of now-pardoned January 6 rioters around the country. Congress must authorize that money for the DOJ to be able to use it, and the only hope for its survival is passage through the reconciliation package.

But many Republicans see this as a complication that will hinder the bill’s passage — even its supporters, like Sen. Tommy Tuberville, who told reporters on Thursday that the fund was a “curveball” that had put delays on the Senate’s plans.

“We want to make sure we get it right. We don’t want to go in there with [senators] not knowing what they’re going to do,” said Tuberville. “Got to have everybody’s vote.”

open image in gallery Acting AG Todd Blanche was on the Hill on Thursday to try and convince a skeptical GOP Senate caucus to approve $1.8B in taxpayer funds to benefit those targeted by the DOJ under Joe Biden ( Reuters )

Sen. John Hoeven of North Dakota confirmed that as of yet, Senate leadership didn’t have the 51 votes necessary to pass a reconcilation package given the disagreements over both the weaponziation fund and other issues.

“We’re still trying to figure out the path to 51”, he said.

Murkowski, speaking to a small gaggle as she left the luncheon, said that the lack of guardrails was her main concern. She pointed to Blanche’s inability to say, repeatedly, that people convicted of fighting with police on January 6 and seeking to harm lawmakers wouldn’t be eligible for compensation under the plan.

open image in gallery Lisa Murkowski is one of the GOP senators who has criticized the lack of planned guardrails around the DOJ's 'weaponization' fund ( Getty )

Tillis, a day before, teed off on the idea.

“Imagine that a fund that is set up to compensate people who assaulted Capitol police officers and other responding agencies, right” Tillis said the day before the meeting with Blanche. “People that had pled guilty to physical acts against the president may actually be able to get compensated. How absurd does that sound coming out of my mouth?"

open image in gallery Thom Tillis, one of the Republicans who has publicly broken with Trump numerous times, ridiculed the DOJ’s plans to compensate January 6 rioters and other targets of prosecution under the Biden DOJ ( Reuters )

Minutes after the news broke of the Senate’s plans to punt the issue, the House cancelled its own plans to hold votes on Friday, effectively signaling that the matter was concluded for the week.

Further complicating the issue for the White House is the administration’s ask for funding to begin the construction of Trump’s planned White House ballroom, which despite the president’s repeated promises that the project is self-funded comes with a $1B price tag for Congress. Republicans are still debating a path forward on that aspect of the reconcilation bill after the Senate parliamentarian — who so often vexed the Biden White House — stripped the language from the draft legislation altogether.

News.content:

The top medical officer at Camp Mystic evacuated herself and her kids and didn’t contact staff as a deadly Texas flood hit last summer, official documents show.

Mary Elizabeth Eastland, the chief health officer at the all-girls Christian camp, “abandoned” campers and her colleagues when water from the Guadalupe River began to flood the campsite in the early morning hours of July 4, 2025, according to an order from the Texas Board of Nursing.

In one of the biggest horrors of the flood that ravaged Kerr County, 25 young campers and two teen counselors were killed.

The order entered Tuesday temporarily suspends Eastland’s nursing license, listing what the board found to be violations during her time at Camp Mystic. Eastland’s attorney, Joshua Fiveson, has said his client denies the allegations against her.

open image in gallery The top medical officer at Camp Mystic evacuated herself and her kids and didn’t contact staff as a deadly Texas flood rolled in last summer, official documents show ( AFP via Getty Images )

By evacuating herself and her kids to higher ground without helping the campers and staff, the board found that she “unnecessarily” exposed others to a “risk of harm.” Eastland is part of the Eastland family, who owns and operates Camp Mystic. She and her husband also serve as co-directors of the campsite.

The board also alleged that Eastland failed to contact the nursing staff to provide instructions and failed to contact emergency services at any time during the flood. She also did not communicate with emergency services after becoming aware that campers and staff were missing, the documents claimed.

Hundreds of first responders combed through Kerr County after the flood, looking for those unaccounted for. In the days that followed, campers’ belongings left behind were photographed. Pops of hot pink scattered throughout piles of clothes and stacked twin-sized mattresses were seen on the lawn of the campsite.

One of the rescuers, Petty Officer Third Class Scott Ruskan with the Coast Guard, recalled finding survivors of the camp’s tragedy, telling The New York Times, “Kids were in pajamas.”

open image in gallery In the days that followed the horrific flood, campers’ belongings were scattered on Camp Mystic’s lawn ( Getty Images )

Eastland’s alleged actions “resulted in the campers and staff not getting the health care, support, and supervision they needed to manage physical harm, emotional harm, psychological harm, and loss of life,” according to the documents.

Attorney Fiveson claimed the board’s order of temporary suspension was handed down without “the benefit of testimony, evidence or a complete investigation,” in a statement shared with The Independent.

He called it a “sad day” for Eastland and “every licensed nurse in Texas.”

“Mrs. Eastland has admirably committed herself to service of others for the last 18 years,” the attorney said, adding that the order is a “premature punishment.”

Fiveson said Eastland “rejects the Board’s allegations and looks forward to defending her rights before the State Office of Administrative Hearings.”

open image in gallery Mary Elizabeth Eastland has had her nursing license temporarily suspended after Texas officials claimed she ‘unnecessarily’ exposed campers to a ‘risk of harm’ ( Getty Images )

The board also alleged that Eastland didn’t have “adequate” emergency plans for campers and staff before the flood.

In a “deceptive” move, Eastland also failed to report the 27 Camp Mystic deaths within 24 hours, as part of the Texas Administrative Code, according to the documents.

The board said that allowing Eastland to continue to practice nursing would be a “continuing and imminent threat to public welfare.”

Camp Mystic decided not to reopen this summer, saying in a statement shared by several news outlets, “No administrative process or summer season should move forward while families continue to grieve, while investigations continue and while so many Texans still carry the pain of last July’s tragedy.”

Cici and Will Steward, whose daughter Cile’s body has still not been found as of late April, said in a statement shared by news outlets, “We are grateful that no child will be placed in the Eastlands’ care this summer.”

News.title: Protesters storm Ebola hospital to retrieve victim’s body
News.content:
Protesters have stormed an Ebola treatment centre in the Democratic Republic of Congo to retrieve the body of a relative, according to local media reports.

Footage circulating online appeared to show parts of Rwampara Hospital engulfed in flames, with plumes of smoke rising above the facility. Gunshots can be heard in the background.

“Angry protesters are setting fire to the tents housing Ebola patients because they want to forcibly retrieve the bodies,” said one man, his face mask pulled below his mouth.

Health authorities oversee the burials of suspected victims in line with strict infection protocols, but this often brings them into conflict with grieving families who want to perform traditional burial rites for their loved ones.

Similar incidents have been a feature of previous Ebola outbreaks, particularly families digging up the bodies of deceased relatives for re-burial – an extremely dangerous act because corpses remain highly contagious for up to a week after death.

In 2022, a cluster of Ebola cases in Uganda was traced back to a family who exhumed their relative at night, undoing the work of a safe burial team in order to give the deceased man a funeral. Within days, at least 23 of the mourners had contracted Ebola and three were dead.

The unrest in Rwampara reportedly erupted on Thursday after the death of a young man suspected of having Ebola at the hospital, which is located around 7.5 miles from Bunia, the capital of the conflict-wracked eastern Ituri province.

News.title: Scientists to monitor British cruise passengers in hantavirus study
News.content:
British passengers repatriated from the cruise ship hit by an outbreak of hantavirus will be monitored for signs of infection as part of a long-term study.

More than 20 Britons who were potentially exposed to the disease on board the MV Hondius have volunteered for the study, which is being run by the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA), the University of Liverpool, the Pandemic Sciences Institute at the University of Oxford, the University of Edinburgh and the University of Glasgow.

It aims to generate robust research on the Andes strain of hantavirus, which is the only variant of the disease known to spread between people but is poorly understood and has no approved vaccine.

After they stop isolating, the volunteers will continue to provide blood samples for testing at Porton Down, the government research facility tasked with studying dangerous pathogens like Ebola, anthrax, and plague.

None of the British passengers who have returned to the UK have so far tested positive for hantavirus. But due to the virus’s long incubation period, which can be up to two months, it is possible they could still become unwell or be asymptomatic carriers of the disease.

One study has previously found that hantavirus could remain in human semen for up to six years and has the potential for sexual transmission, even after a person has recovered.

If a male patient tests positive for the virus, investigators will also look to test their semen for ongoing signs of infection.

“If we do have a case, we can study that in more detail and think about the mechanisms of the disease and how we can treat that disease better,” said Professor Lance Turtle, Chair in Immunity and Infectious Diseases at the University of Liverpool and Joint Chief Investigator in the study.

News.title: All-in-one chocolate cake
News.content:
Step

Spread the buttercream on one layer of cake – use a spatula or a palette knife – then put the other layer on top. Using a clean spatula or palette knife, spread the chocolate glaze on top of this layer (or drizzle it over) and encourage it down the sides of the cake. Neaten it all the way round with the palette knife. Leave to set a little before serving.

News.title: Welsh cakes
News.content: I’d never tasted a Welsh cake until I went to St Dogmaels local producers’ market for the BBC, some years back. I had them hot off the griddle with butter. They’re fragile and melting and much better than any scone. They’re also easy, quick to make and inexpensive, so just right for rainy-day weekend baking (when you bake a cake for someone else but want a treat for everyone in your house too), or even a midweek pick-me-up.

News.title: Lemon tart with blueberries
News.content:
The pastry here is from the California chef Lindsey Shere and it’s wonderful – thin and buttery and almost biscuity. You make it in a slightly different way, creaming the butter and sugar for it and then smearing it little by little with the heel of your hand (the French term is ‘fraisage’) once the flour has been added. There are good how-to videos online for the pastry method.

Do follow the chilling times and only add the amount of blueberries given here, otherwise they’ll bleed too much.

Sports.title: England’s predicted 26-man World Cup squad as Palmer and Maguire lead host of senior stars axed with Toney surprise pick
Sports.content:
THOMAS TUCHEL has made some incredibly big calls for his World Cup squad.

England‘s official 26-man squad for the tournament, which will take place in Canada, Mexico and the United States, will be officially announced on Friday.





But SunSport has learned of several glaring omissions from the squad, which have stunned Three Lions fans across the world.

The biggest names who will be watching the tournament from their sofa – or their sun loungers – are undoubtedly Harry Maguire and Cole Palmer.

Phil Foden is another glaring omission from the squad, as is Nottingham Forest‘s Morgan Gibbs-White.

Equally as stunning as the omissions of Maguire and Palmer are the inclusions of Ivan Toney, who is still plying his trade in Saudi Arabia, and Brentford‘s Jordan Henderson.



The troops Tuchel will deploy next month to try to end the nation’s 60 years of hurt are currently the talk of footie fans up and down the country.

But SunSport is on hand to reveal the players who, going off the omissions from the squad, are dead certs to be on the plane next month.



Goalkeepers

Jordan Pickford is expected to maintain his status as England’s No.1, with Dean Henderson and James Trafford serving as his deputies.

SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Defenders

Tuchel is expected to take NINE defenders to North America, the most experienced of those being John Stones.

Stones will be the elder statesman for fellow centre-backs Ezri Konsa, Jarrell Quansah, Marc Guehi and Dan Burn to call on.

Nico O’Reilly, Myles Lewis-Skelly, Reece James and Tino Livramento are expected to make up the squad’s full-back contingent.

Midfielders

Tuchel has seemingly gone for four central midfielders, with Henderson, 35, being the most experienced of the lot.



New Premier League champion Declan Rice will likely start ahead of Hendo and could be partnered in the middle of the park by either Elliot Anderson or Kobbie Mainoo.

Forwards

Arsenal trio Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke and Bukayo Saka will vie for starting berths on the wings and just behind the lone striker.

They’ll face competition from Newcastle‘s Anthony Gordon and Manchester United‘s Marcus Rashford, the latter of whom had a stunning loan spell with Barcelona this season

Strikers

Although it’s not been officially announced, the only guaranteed name in the squad list was that of the nation’s all-time leading goalscorer, Harry Kane.



Aston Villa hitman Ollie Watkins is also set to be on the plane, and surely, given the fact he’s been playing at a higher level, will be further up in the pecking order than Saudi-based striker Toney.

Sports.title: After sexy Abbey Clancy ad recalls wild days of 2006 World Cup we ask were Wags REALLY to blame for England’s exit?
Sports.content:
SUITABLY well-oiled, the Wags arrived at Garibaldi’s bar in the sedate German spa town of Baden-Baden and ordered more champagne.

Some were soon dancing on tables amid shattered bubbly flutes as Coleen McLoughlin belted out an ode to her fiancé: “There’s Only One Wayne Rooney.”





Not to be outdone, Elen Rives serenaded the bar with a ditty for her then other half: “Super Frankie Lampard.”

Partying until 4am, and fuelled by bottles of Moet champagne drunk with strawberry syrup, glasses of vodka and Red Bull and shots of sambuca, the raucous party bellowed: “We’re not going home, we’re not going home.”

The bawdy singalong included a turn from the improbably named Neville Neville — father to defenders Phil and Gary — who attempted a rendition of God Save The Queen.

The players’ dad would later be pictured in newspapers clutching a replica World Cup, his exploits in the town appearing under a headline Neville Neville in Baden-Baden.



And striker Peter Crouch’s girlfriend Abbey Clancy, who this week stripped to a thong to promote a Wag-themed clothing collection for US brand Juicy Couture, would be sent home in disgrace after old pictures emerged of her snorting cocaine.

Meanwhile, a 20-minute drive into the Black Forest mountains at the secluded Schloss Buhlerhohe Hotel, the Wags’ husbands — England’s so-called Golden Generation of footballers — were trying to kick-start their stuttering 2006 World Cup campaign.

Two tortuous wins against Paraguay and Trinidad and Tobago and a heart-stopping draw against Sweden in the group stage hardly justified England’s position as second- favourites to win the tournament behind Brazil.

Ecuador awaited in the round of 16 knockout phase for a squad that included David Beckham, Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard, Ashley Cole, Rio Ferdinand, John Terry, Wayne Rooney and Joe Cole.



And yet it was the wives and families who were stealing all the headlines with their exploits in what was starting to resemble a high-end hen do.

Then there was the shopping. Some of the group had spent £57,000 in one hour in designer clothes stores.

German tabloid Bild sneered: “They spend more in ten minutes than most of us do on our wardrobe in half a lifetime.”

And Spanish paper ABC trumpeted of the credit card spree: “Not even the stores of Vuitton and Gucci can keep up with the daily attack of the hooligans with Visas.”

It was the high watermark of Wag culture which featured in recent BBC documentary England 2006: The Golden Generation — and it is an era that Abbey Clancy, at least, is ready to resurrect. One skimpy T-shirt from the mum-of-four’s new range features the slogan “Juicy Wag”.



It’s quite a rehabilitation for the Wives And Girlfriends tag after Baden-Baden left them open to accusations that their behaviour had harmed the England team.

So did the Wags really derail the chance of glory for one of the most gifted Three Lions squads, or were they scapegoated after some shambolic performances on the pitch?

Then-manager Sven-Goran Eriksson had fought to base the team in Baden-Baden and for the Wags to be offered the chance to stay in the town.



Of the 23-man squad, only Aaron Lennon, 19, didn’t bring a partner. All invited family members, with the England entourage swelling to 110.

They were led by Victoria Beckham (dubbed Queen Wag) while Girls Aloud’s Cheryl Cole (then Tweedy), and Eriksson’s partner Nancy Dell’Olio also held court. For the Press, it was an irresistible mix of glamour and celebrity. There was the occasional football match too.

‘Isolated places’When Baden-Baden was unveiled as England’s base camp, Eriksson praised its “marvellous atmosphere, with some wonderful restaurants and cafes”.

They were ominous words — yet the FA believed the pretty town, with a population just over 55,000, was an ideal retreat for the squad and their families.

Then-FA chairman Brian Barwick recalled: “The (team) hotel and training base were miles out of town. We were up a hill and I thought it was one of the most isolated places I’d ever been to. We knew the players’ wives could stay down in the town in the Brenners Park Hotel and see their partners occasionally but generally be free to do what they wanted.”



The build-up to the tournament was dominated by Rooney’s race to be fit after breaking his fourth metatarsal in his right foot.

But after the first game — a cagey 1-0 win with a deflected own goal against Paraguay — the Wags took centre stage.

At the bar of their Brenners Park Hotel, peach bellinis in sugared champagne flutes were downed while Frederico’s resident pianist was being drowned out by a chorus of We Are The Champions. Pizzas and chips were served on silver platters followed by more peach bellinis, wine and beer.

While most of the group headed for bed around midnight.

But Coleen, Elen, Joe Cole’s now wife Carly Zucker, David Beckham’s sister Joanne and Steven Gerrard’s partner Alex Curran headed for Garibaldi’s — the restaurant and nightclub which would become Wags party central for three weeks.



Before the fun came to an end at 3am, the party downed £300-worth of Moet champagne and nine vodka Red Bulls, with Elen dancing on a bench in stilettos.

Baden-Baden’s Gucci and Hermes stores had bought in an extra £200,000 in stock, and much of it was snapped up by the Wags.

Bild newspaper wrote: “It has turned into Shopping-Shopping in Baden-Baden.”



A Fleet Street photographer described the women’s daily routine: “Morning coffee or maybe a run in town, shopping, back to the hotel, then on the p**s.

“It was full-on. They got no rest, so neither did we. Our rest days were when we got sent to cover the England matches.”

Initially reporting in other parts of Germany, after the Three Lions beat Ecuador to set up a quarter-final against Portugal, I too was drawn to Baden-Baden like a wasp to a plastic cup of stale lager.

Sun snapper Arthur Edwards and I made straight for hallowed Garibaldi’s and were rewarded with a front-page story as an extra 1,230 pints of lager were delivered for the thirsty England party.

Owner Carmine Tortora told us: “I’m delighted England beat Ecuador and hope they can stay in the competition as long as possible. I am Germany’s happiest bar owner.



“It’s been our best-ever two weeks of business.”

It didn’t take long to spot various Wags parading around the town.

I remember seeing a bewildered-looking Theo Walcott who Eriksson had brought along as a wild card despite not having started a Premier League game.

Then on July 1 England met Porttugal in Gelsenkirchen. Beckham was forced off with an Achilles injury early in the second half. In the 62nd minute, Rooney was sent off for stepping on Ricardo Carvalho.

Then Cristiano Ronaldo — Rooney’s Manchester United teammate — sprinted to the ref and demanded a red card.



Rooney went and the cameras caught Ronaldo winking at his bench. It was over.

Back in Baden-Baden there was time for a quick £30,000 shopping spree by the Wags and a last drink in Garibaldi’s.

Despite losing Beckham and Michael Owen to injury and Rooney admitting he had not recovered properly from his broken bone, some in the FA corridors of power blamed the Wags for World Cup failure.



Last year Gary Neville said on the Stick To Football podcast: “I can only describe it as an absolute circus. It wasn’t with the wives (that I was annoyed) but the whole organisation of the trip.

“There were stories breaking every day. ‘They’ve eaten here today,’ or ‘They’ve shopped here’ — it was just a constant distraction.

Sports.title: ‘Deplorable’ Southampton ‘pressured intern to spy on rivals in Tonda Eckert-backed plot’, EFL Spygate findings reveal
Sports.content:
“DEPLORABLE” Southampton LIED about recording opposition training sessions before boss Tonda Eckert admitted his key role in spying after evidence was uncovered.

The Saints are also guilty of putting pressure on junior staff members to spy on rivals.





The South Coast outfit are in meltdown after the FA launched its own investigation into the Spygate saga that has rocked the club – threatening even more savage punishments.

As Sun Sport exclusively revealed last week, Eckert could face a possible ban, potentially up to 18 months, along with any other figures responsible for the club’s spying missions. While his part in the whole operation leaves his position in serious doubt.

Southampton are already reeling after being sensationally booted out of the play-offs and hit with a four-point deduction for next season for spying on Middlesbrough, Ipswich and Oxford.

St Mary’s chiefs saw a desperate, last-gasp appeal rejected by an independent panel on Wednesday night, completely torching their dreams of a £215MILLION promotion jackpot.

But a fresh bombshell rocked the spying Saints as the EFL’s release of the written reasons as to why an independent commission expelled them revealed how they initially lied about the snooping and how junior staff members were pressured to spy on opposition teams, which was all authorised by their German head coach Eckert, 33.

The commission noted: “It involved far more than innocent activity and a particularly deplorable approach in its use of junior members of staff to conduct the clandestine observations at the direction of senior personnel.

“There was transmission and internal dissemination and analysis of footage and observations. The Commission is not persuaded that this is an exceptional case in which there is evidence that no use was made of the material and therefore no sporting advantage.

“The Commission consider that the evidence demonstrates that the output of the observations fed into analysis conducted by the team, it was discussed with Mr Eckert and others and it was sought so as to inform the strategy for the match. Mr Eckert accepted, as he must, that information such as team selection and injuries is sensitive information which a club would wish to keep private in the build up to a game.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

“He also accepted that he had specifically authorised the observations to obtain information about formation (in the Oxford United Incident) and about the availability of a key player (in the Middlesbrough Incident).

“We were unimpressed by suggestions on the part of some of the (Southampton’s) witnesses that they were unaware that these actions were in breach of the Rules. (Southampton) is a member of the EFL and has agreed to be bound by the Rules.”



Sun Sport revealed the shock photo of the moment intern analyst William Salt was caught red-handed recording Boro train less than 48 hours before the first leg of the semi final.

But the report revealed that Salt refused to dress up and disguise himself in an Eastleigh FC kit in an attempt to film Ipswich as he “described the pressure” to the commission that he was placed under.

It added: “The EFL submitted that the evidence supported the view that the observations were authorised at a senior level and that the task was delegated to the intern in relation to the Middlesbrough Incident and the Oxford Incident. He declined to be involved in the Ipswich incident. We heard evidence from the intern who described the pressure he was placed under.

“Such staff were in a vulnerable position without job security and with limited ability to object to or resist the instructions given to them.

“We have concluded that there was, on the part of the respondent (Southampton), a contrived and determined plan from the top down to gain a competitive advantage in competitions of real significance by deliberate attendance at opposition training grounds for the purpose of obtaining tactical and selection information.”



Meanwhile, Southampton captain Taylor Harwood-Bellis has broken his silence on Spygate – and claims he would not have mocked Boro star Aidan Morris with a binoculars celebration had he known the severity of the scandal.

After addressing the squad’s heartbreak, he added: “I’d also like to put on record that, had I known the severity of the situation, I would never have done what I did on the pitch.”

The chaotic events have also led to Southampton players contemplating suing their own club for potential loss of earnings or ripping up their contracts while Eckert now faces the sack for orchestrating, approving and overseeing the spying.

Elsewhere, Hull owner Acun Ilicali considered his own legal action to argue that his side should get automatically promoted without the need to play the final – because Boro have already lost.

Saints legend Matt Le Tissier, though, fumed at the ruling.



He told SunSport: “Personally I try to put a neutral hat on but I feel like the punishment does feel a bit disproportionate.

“It feels like you’ve been put on trial for murder when all you’ve done is stolen a Mars bar from the corner shop.

“You could say it’s a 50-50 chance of whether we go up or not. So I’d probably say it’s like a £100million fine.

“It’s a rule talking about something that gets you literally a microscopic advantage over a team.”

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo bursts into tears as footie legend, 41, wins first Al-Nassr trophy after three years in Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
CRISTIANO RONALDO burst into tears after finally ending his agonising three-year silverware drought with Al-Nassr.

The Portuguese icon was the hero as he fired his side to a 4-1 win over Damac at the Alawwal Park in Riyadh.





The win and the three points confirmed Al-Nassr‘s place as champions of the Saudi Pro League.

Ronaldo, 41, and co headed into the match needing at least a point to hold off rivals Al-Hilal – after seeing the championship slip through their fingers, quite literally, in dramatic scenes against their title rivals last week

That night, Al-Nassr goalkeeper Bento made a catastrophic error in the last seconds of added time to fumble into his own net to hand Al-Hilal a 1-1 draw.

But Ronaldo and Co left nothing to chance this time as the Manchester United legend netted twice in a title-winning rout.

Former Liverpool star Sadio Mane opened the scoring in the 31st minute before Kinsley Coman doubled the lead after the break.

Morlaye Sylla nabbed one back for Damac before Ronaldo stepped up to put the result beyond doubt.



The five-time Ballon d’Or winner netted in the 62nd and 80th minutes to give Al-Nassr a three-goal cushion.

His first goal was the pick of the bunch as he managed to score a rare free-kick from a tight angle.

Despite his explosive goalscoring form since making the mega-money move to the Middle East, team trophies had frustratingly evaded the serial winner.

But after three long years of trying, the legendary attacker can finally call himself a champion once again.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK



The triumph means Ronaldo adds yet another domestic crown to his glittering museum, making him a champion in four different top-flight leagues.

He didn’t quite finish the match on the turf, as boss Jorge Jesus subbed him off in the closing stages to receive a standing ovation from adoring fans.

As the final whistle approached, the emotional superstar completely broke down on the bench as the reality of the achievement hit home.

But Ronaldo was soon at the centre of celebrations as he banged a drum for chanting supporters, surrounded by his team-mates.



Next he was flanked by proud partner Georgina Rodriguez and his kids before going up to lift the trophy.

Ronaldo famously made the switch to the Gulf state after a bitter, high-profile fallout with former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag.



He penned a staggering contract worth a mind-blowing £178million-a-year to lead the Saudi football revolution.

And he has certainly kept his side of the bargain on the pitch, defying his advancing years with an incredible goal return.

The goal-machine has plundered 123 goals for Al-Nassr in just 142 games — a mere 18 strikes short of his total United tally.

Astonishingly, he has achieved the breathtaking number in 204 fewer appearances than he made for the Red Devils.



Ronaldo has racked up 28 goals in 30 league games this term, but he will remarkably miss out on the Golden Boot.

That honour will go to former Brentford striker Ivan Toney, who hit 32 goals in 32 appearances for Al-Ahli, in the process earning himself a surprise spot in England’s World Cup squad.

Sports.title: Celtic vs Hearts referee ‘ended match without blowing whistle’ as Scottish FA reveal little-known rule
Sports.content:
CELTIC’S controversial title-clinching victory over Hearts was brought to a bizarre end without the referee ever blowing the final whistle.

The Hoops ran out 3-1 winners to miraculously land their 56th Scottish league title — but the historic achievement was instantly overshadowed by total pandemonium.





Chaos erupted at Celtic Park when thousands of jubilant fans stormed the pitch after Callum Osmand netted a dramatic third goal in the 97th minute.

Despite there being around 30 seconds left on the clock, referee Don Robertson never restarted the action as the turf vanished under a sea of green and white.

In the terrifying aftermath, Hearts claimed there were reports that some of their players had been assaulted on the pitch.

The Edinburgh club slammed the “menacing and threatening” scenes before the Jambos were rushed out of the stadium straight onto the team bus for their own safety.



Hearts chiefs released a blistering statement questioning why the game was halted by a security breach rather than a whistle from the match officials.

While some fans insisted Hearts should actually have been awarded the three points – and the league title that would have come with them – with the game abandoned due to the fan invasion.

But SPFL bosses have fired back, insisting the match was correctly ended.

The Scottish FA have now released the official VAR audio, which proves Robertson called time AFTER the full eight minutes of injury time had been played.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Sensationally, the audio also revealed that Hearts manager Derek McInnes had actually begged officials to stop the game due to major safety concerns for his players.

The referee complied, bringing the curtain down on the match despite never actually placing the whistle to his lips.

The dramatic move is fully protected by a little-known IFAB rule which gives referees power over the match clock.

A statement from the Scottish FA read: “In the interests of transparency, we are happy to set out the facts.



“Regarding references to a ‘premature ending of the match’, the Scottish FA’s Chief Governance Officer, Gary Booth, the Head of Refereeing, William Collum, and VAR Manager Martin Atkinson reviewed the audio-visual footage of the period in question on Monday at the club’s request, with Mr Paterson in attendance.

“While it was the agreed intention for this meeting to be conducted privately, recent statements have compelled us to consider the public interest in providing clarification and chronology.

“It was made clear at that meeting that the match official, Don Robertson, took the correct action in ending the game.

“We note there has been speculation regarding the blowing of a final whistle.



“The Laws of the Game require the referee to signal the end of the match, but do not prescribe the method of that signal.

“In the context of what unfolded – which is verified by the footage and the Match Incident Report submitted to the Scottish FA – the match official clearly communicated that the match was ended and not abandoned.

“In addition, the match clock does not stop when a goal is scored.

“The footage shows that when the match official confirms the game has ended, the clock is at 53.07 [98.07], more than the minimum additional time of eight minutes signalled.



“It was also apparent from the audio that this decision was taken following dialogue with the Hearts Head Coach, who had intimated concerns over player safety.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“For the avoidance of doubt, Law 5 of the IFAB Laws of the Game state that ‘the decisions of the referee regarding facts connected with play are final’.

“We fully support the decisive action taken by Don Robertson and his team to end the game.”

Sports.title: England to call up forgotten star, 30, to World Cup squad after long exile as Cole Palmer is dropped
Sports.content:
IVAN TONEY is set to head to the World Cup – despite plying his trade in the Saudi Pro League.

The former Brentford hitman is on course to win the Saudi golden boot this season having scored 32 goals for Al-Ahli.





The 30-year-old has bagged a whopping 49 GOALS in all competitions this campaign.

And his fine form has seen Thomas Tuchel reward him with a spot in his 26-man squad for this summer‘s World Cup, which gets underway next month.

England fans were stunned by the news of Toney’s inclusion in the squad, which will officially be announced on Friday.

One wrote on X: “Ivan Toney is crazy.”



Another said: “Ivan Toney back in the squad… IDK what this man is doing.”

A third wrote: “No f***ing way is Ivan ‘Sunday league’ Toney going to the World Cup.”

One remarked: “Ivan Toney in the England squad My eyes are bleeding.”

Another chimed in: “IVAN TONEY, WTF?”



Anyone who thinks this squad can win World Cup needs their head tested, says Charlie Wyett THOMAS TUCHEL has properly put his b******s on the line with this England squad, writes Charlie Wyett. And the German is going to end up being hailed as a genius for the group of players he has selected – or a disaster. Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Harry Maguire, Morgan Gibbs-White, Adam Wharton and Levi Colwill are just some of the players missing. And the big shock inclusion is Ivan Toney whose only appearance for Tuchel was as an 88th minute sub against Senegal after he failed to impress in training at last summer’s post-season camp in Girona. Individually, you can see why some of the players have missed out as the likes of Foden, in particular, do not deserve to be included. But Maguire has been in good form for Manchester United and once he got a recall in March, he obviously thought he was back in. England certainly need players of his experience which is why it is the right call to stick with Jordan Henderson. Tuchel needs to be applauded for his bravery but this squad does not look particularly settled and I would still have also included Luke Shaw. Also, Dan Burn is incredibly lucky to be in this squad and the same goes for Tino Livramento. The defence looks bang-average and anyone who thinks this squad can win the World Cup needs to get their head tested. Harry Kane yesterday claimed the squad has never been stronger but he is surely having a laugh. And the fact England will still go into the tournament as one of the bookies’ favourites is a joke. Tuchel called the players via phone between 4pm and 8pm to explain his decision while the official unveiling is at 10am tomorrow. At 11am, he will talk to the media and his views will be intriguing.

Tuchel brought Toney back into the England fold last May after he finished runner-up to Cristiano Ronaldo in last season’s race for the Saudi Golden Boot.

The German said of Toney’s return: “He deserves to be with us and I am convinced because he scored over 20 goals for his team this season.

“He won a major title with the Asian Champions League, he had a big contribution with goals and assists.

“I said last time [in March] that I would try to put a visit in my schedule [to Saudi Arabia] which I didn’t make, so I thought bring him [Toney] over and let him travel with us.”



But Toney has not featured in any of the the last FOUR squads.

Toney is seemingly take the place of Cole Palmer this summer.

The Chelsea ace has paid the price for a poor season by his standards, in which he scored ten goals and provided three assists in 33 appearances in all competitions.

The 24-year-old bagged 18 goals and racked up 14 assists in 52 appearances last season, in which he helped fire Chelsea to Conference League glory.

Cristiano Ronaldo breaks down in tears as Al-Nassr finally win Saudi Pro League title

Al-Nassr have won the Saudi Pro League for the first time since Cristiano Ronaldo joined the club in 2022, as they pummelled Damac 4-1 on Thursday to wrap up the title

A relieved Cristiano Ronaldo broke down in tears before finally getting his hands on the Saudi Pro League title. Al-Nassr were crowned champions following a resounding 4-1 win at home to Damac on Thursday in which their captain scored twice.

‌



Ronaldo, 41, has had a painstaking wait for his first major trophy in Saudi Arabia, including losing a cup final on Saturday. That was the second heartbreak the Portugal captain had suffered in the space of five days.

‌



In their penultimate league game against second-placed Al-Hilal, his side were seconds away from sealing the title before they conceded a stoppage-time equaliser courtesy of a defensive mixup. Ronaldo and his team-mates subsequently had to wait until the final day, but they've now got their hands on the trophy.

‌



After goals from Sadio Mane and Kingsley Coman set Al-Nassr on their way, Damac threatened a comeback by scoring before the hour mark. But within five minutes, Ronaldo netted the first of his two goals from a free-kick and sealed the win.

Ivan Toney has received a sensational World Cup call-up.

‌



England boss Thomas Tuchel will include Toney in his 26 man squad when he names it on Friday. The 30-year-old has been in the International wilderness for the past 12 months but has scored 42 goals in 37 games for Al Ahli in the Saudi Pro League.

‌



Mirror Sport revealed on May 11 that Tuchel was considering bringing back the ex-Brentford striker and he will get the nod amid some huge casualties.

‌



Phil Foden, Cole Palmer and Harry Maguire have all been axed while Ollie Watkins, Noni Madueke, Jordan Henderson, Kobbie Mainoo are expected to make the cut.

OPINION John Cross Thomas Tuchel has been brutal with England World Cup squad calls - now they must pay off

Watkins was axed from England’s last squad in March but the Aston Villa striker has been rewarded for his outstanding form since then, including winning the Europa League final.

‌



Foden has missed out because of a lack of game time at Manchester City while Palmer is also out because he has struggled for form and fitness this season.

Luke Shaw is out while his Manchester United teammate Maguire has also been axed by ruthless Tuchel and that would surely end his England career.

Maguire, 33, has enjoyed a terrific second half of the season and hoped to make it despite Tuchel insisting in March that he was effectively SIXTH choice centre half behind the likes of Dan Burn as well as Marc Guehi, Ezri Konsa and John Stones.

‌



View 2 Images Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is also in Thomas Tuchel's World Cup squad (Image: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Maguire issued a statement and said: “I was confident I could have played a major part this summer for my country after the season I’ve had. I’ve been left shocked and gutted by the decision. I wish the players all the best.”

Tuchel is naming 26 players on Friday and they will fly to Florida on June 1 but Arsenal’s contingent will not join up until later that week.

‌



England begin their World Cup campaign in Dallas against Croatia on June 17.

Sports.title: Harry Maguire's mum 'absolutely disgusted' after Man Utd star left out of England squad
Sports.content:
Harry Maguire's mum 'absolutely disgusted' after Man Utd star left out of England squad

Harry Maguire has been left out of England's World Cup squad by Thomas Tuchel, despite enjoying an impressive second half of the season under Michael Carrick at Manchester United

View Image Harry Maguire's mum has taken to social media (Image: zoemaguirewilkinson/Instagram)

Harry Maguire's mum says that she's 'absolutely disgusted' by her son's omission from the England squad. Maguire, 33, has missed out on Thomas Tuchel's 26-man squad which will be announced on Friday morning.

‌



But news regarding the Manchester United star emerged on Thursday night and he soon confirmed his axe on social media amid outrage from fans who believe that he should've been called up. In a post on Instagram, Maguire commented: "I was confident I could of played a major part this summer for my country after the season I've had.

‌



"I've been left shocked and gutted by the decision. I've loved nothing more than putting that shirt on and representing my country over the years. I wish the players, all the best this summer."

‌



His mum, Zoe, didn't need nearly as many words to express her opinion. On X, she wrote: "Absolutely disgusted."

WORLD CUP LEGENDS: The stars who lit up football's greatest tournament - Buy the Special Edition today

Cole Palmer and Phil Foden among the big casualties as England squad calls made READ MORE :

One of his brothers, Joe, also fumed: "This might possibly be the worst decision I've ever seen in my life. No words."

‌



Tuchel will explain his decision regarding Maguire at a press conference on Friday, and the centre-back isn't the only big name to miss out. Cole Palmer, Phil Foden, Luke Shaw and Morgan Gibbs-White are also among the high-profile omissions.

It was Maguire's mum who 'started crying' when he was recalled to the England squad in March following an 18-month absence. Discussing his recall, the 33-year-old said: "It's amazing. It's something I've missed.

"When you don't get picked, when you've been a regular for six or seven years, it's tough. I spoke to the manager and he told me I was in.

‌

Sports.title: Taylor Harwood-Bellis makes statement on Spygate binoculars gesture as Southampton kicked out of play-offs
Sports.content:
Taylor Harwood-Bellis makes statement on Spygate binoculars gesture as Southampton kicked out of play-offs

Southampton were thrown out of the Championship playoffs this week and saw their appeal quashed

View 2 Images Taylor Harwood-Bellis has spoken out after Southampton were thrown out of the playoffs and Middlesbrough were reinstated. (Image: Kieran McManus/Shutterstock)

Southampton captain Taylor Harwood-Bellis has claimed that he wouldn't have mocked Spygate had he understood the seriousness of the situation. The former Manchester City prospect made a binoculars gesture after the Saints scored a dramatic late winner in the Championship play-off semi-final victory over Middlesbrough.

‌



Tonda Eckert's side were expelled from the competition and saw their appeal rejected after breaching English Football League (EFL) regulations. Southampton had secured their spot in the playoff final against Hull City after defeating Boro 1-0 over two legs after extra-time. But the contest between the two sides was marred by allegations of spying by the Saints.

‌



The South Coast outfit were subsequently charged, admitted the breach and during a hearing this week confessed to two additional breaches of spying earlier in the campaign. The independent commission expelled the club from the playoffs, reinstating Boro, and docked four points for next season. Southampton appealed but saw their hopes of reversing the verdict dashed on Wednesday.

‌



Harwood-Bellis has been compelled to backtrack on his actions as the Independent Commission's ruling left both him and the squad "gutted, disappointed and heartbroken".

In a post to Instagram, he said: "It's been nothing but an honour to walk this team out and represent every fan watching in the stands, so it feels right that I speak to you guys directly about what has unfolded this week. As players, we are absolutely gutted, disappointed, and heartbroken that it's come to this.

Tonda Eckert condemned for 'deplorable' Southampton Spygate campaign as EFL release full verdict READ MORE :

"We worked so hard as a group to provide the football that you fans deserve. For those of us involved in the relegation, it only fuelled our comeback. We knew what it felt like to play in the Premier League, and we were driven by the belief that we could bring that back to you all.

‌



"I'd also like to put on record that, had I known the severity of the situation, I would never have done what I did on the pitch. In the moment, it was meant as a bit of fun in a situation that we as players were not informed about."

"As fans, you've been unbelievable. Our unbeaten run was driven by your passionate support. We didn't start the season strongly, yet you still stood by us and believed in every single one of us."

View 2 Images Taylor Harwood-Bellis during a Southampton FC training session (Image: Matt Watson, Southampton FC via Getty Images)

‌



"We can be proud that we battled through a tough Championship season together, and I'll always be grateful for the support you gave us every step of the way. Thank you. Enjoy your summer, Saints."

The controversy emerged seven years after Leeds United's spying scandal sent shockwaves through English football, yet Southampton's attempts to gain an unfair advantage proved equally damaging to the sport's integrity, bringing the game into disrepute.

Fresh reports have surfaced in the wake of the spying scandal, with Southampton allegedly disguising themselves in Eastleigh colours while Ipswich Town were preparing at the National League side's Hampshire base ahead of their clash with Saints in April.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Saints confessed to spying on Oxford United prior to their encounter last year, though it ultimately proved fruitless as they suffered a 2-1 defeat. Eckert is facing intense pressure following the independent panel's ruling and is now under investigation by the Football Association (FA), while also confronting the possibility of dismissal for authorising the covert operation.

On Wednesday, it emerged that Southampton players were considering legal action should the appeal against expulsion be rejected due to loss of earnings. It was reported that players forfeited financial rewards including promotion bonuses and wage increases.

‌



In a statement following the rejection of their appeal, Southampton said: "Southampton Football Club has this evening been informed that the EFL's League Arbitration Panel has upheld the sanctions imposed earlier this week. As a result, the club will not participate in Saturday's Championship Play-Off Final.

"This is an extremely disappointing outcome for everybody connected with Southampton Football Club. We know how painful this moment will be for our supporters, players, staff, commercial partners and the wider community who have given so much backing to the team throughout the season and we apologise once again to everyone impacted by this.

‌



"While we fully acknowledge the seriousness of this matter and the scrutiny that has followed, the club has consistently believed the original sporting sanction was disproportionate, a view that has been widely shared by many in the football community over the last 24 hours.

"We would like to place on record our sincere thanks to our supporters for the support, patience and loyalty they have shown throughout an incredibly difficult period. We will share information as soon as possible in relation to ticket refunds for those who bought tickets to Wembley.

"Southampton Football Club has a proud history and strong foundations, but it is clear that trust now needs to be rebuilt. That work begins immediately. The club will reflect carefully on the events that have led to this point, learn from them and take the necessary steps to move forward responsibly.

"While tonight is a painful moment, this football club will respond with humility, accountability and determination to put things right."
